messages:
maria (PM): quick sync — customers asking for per-route latency alerts + SLO-based alerting in the console. putting a lightweight PRD stub here for scope decisions.

maria (PM): problem: teams need alerts that map to customer-facing routes and SLOs, not infra-only signals. want: per-route SLO creation, simple alert rules, and retention controls so alerts tie back to traces and logs.

drew (Eng): +1. main engineering concern: cardinality. per-route + per-tenant metrics can blow up. we'll need default aggregation tiers and a cap.

sam (SRE): agree on cardinality. also need to define noise budget and escalation paths. who owns alert burn rate? ops vs customer? :thinking_face:

maria (PM): draft scope options: 1) Minimal: SLOs at service-level + per-route label option (no per-tenant). 2) Mid: per-route + sampling + retention tiers. 3) Full: per-tenant per-route with unlimited retention (enterprise). Which one should we aim for GA?

aisha (Design): UX note: creation flow must hide complexity. default templates for common SLO types (p50/p95 latency, error-rate). show estimated query cost when creating.

drew (Eng): technical tradeoffs: Mid-level seems feasible for Q3 if we add: - sampling (1p50 and 1p95 exemplar sampling), - retention tiering backend (7/30/90 days), - explicit cardinality limits enforced at ingest.

sam (SRE): + Mid. For alerts, acceptance criteria need to include noise reduction tests: simulated traffic with route churn, ensure <2% false alert rate on baseline workload.

maria (PM): adding acceptance criteria (draft):
```
- Users can create SLOs scoped to service or named route.
- Alerts can be configured with threshold + burn-rate + notification targets.
- Console displays estimated query cost and retention window at creation.
- Default retention tiers: 7d (free), 30d (standard), 90d (enterprise).
- System enforces cardinality: max 10k active route-labels per org; soft cap warnings at 8k.
- On route deletion, SLOs show a deprecation notice for 30 days before hard delete.
```

drew (Eng): edge cases to call out: route name collisions (different services with same route path), rapid route churn during deploys, and metric backfills causing retroactive alerts. We should ensure alert windows anchor to ingestion time, not event time.

aisha (Design): UX edgecases: when SLO references a route that later gets renamed — show history and link the old name. Also need a compact alert overview for oncall.

sam (SRE): monitoring/ops checklist: provide a dry-run mode for new alerts that simulates noisy traffic and returns expected firing count. Also require a per-org alert mute policy for maintenance windows.

maria (PM): prioritization proposal: ship Mid as GA for self-serve. Minimal as immediate beta toggle to unblock customers. Full reserved for enterprise roadmap (post-GA). Thoughts?

drew (Eng): agree. suggest rollout plan: beta -> opt-in orgs (2 customers) -> GA with capacitiy guardrails. Also we need telemetry events for usage and cost impacts.

sam (SRE): add runbook items and one canary org with synthetic workloads for 2 weeks pre-GA. ops-bot: create canary ticket?

ops-bot: created ticket INF-3421: "Alerting SLO canary — synthetic traffic and burn-rate tests" assigned to @sam, due 1829906000.

maria (PM): next steps: I'll turn this into a short PRD doc with the acceptance criteria and rollout plan. @drew can you estimate eng effort for Mid (rough ballpark)? @sam pls scope canary runbook. aisha will produce a 2-screen UI mock for creation + overview.

drew (Eng): ballpark: 6-8 sprints across infra + console + metrics teams if we do Mid in parallel with retention tiering. can tighten after spike.

sam (SRE): I'll draft the canary runbook today and post link here.

aisha (Design): will share mocks by EOD Wed.

maria (PM): thanks all — scheduling a 30m sync for Thursday to finalize. :thumbsup:
